Ui.Script:
-- The timer switch (ref uvar, UIOptionsFrame.lua l.21/104 — its `default = "0"`). This -- assignment is the ONLY statement of our default: the saved chunk executes over it at load -- (1128) and the Interface page's row captures it as its Defaults value at OnLoad, which -- runs first. "1" because the director asked for visible timers (0255) — the divergence is -- written down once, here, and Defaults honours it rather than the reference's table. SHOW_BUFF_DURATIONS = "1" RegisterForSave("SHOW_BUFF_DURATIONS")
-- The reference's flash cadence + thresholds (BuffFrame.lua l.1-14). An aura in its last 31s -- pulses between full and BUFF_MIN_ALPHA; its duration text turns highlight-white under 60s. BUFF_FLASH_TIME_ON = 0.75 BUFF_FLASH_TIME_OFF = 0.75 BUFF_MIN_ALPHA = 0.3 BUFF_WARNING_TIME = 31 BUFF_DURATION_WARNING_TIME = 60
-- The dispel-class border tints (BuffFrame.lua l.9-14); "none" is the undispellable red the -- debuff overlay wears by default. GetPlayerBuffDispelType's return keys this table — it -- hands back the SpellDispelType.dbc name, or nil, never "" and never "none". DebuffTypeColor = { ["none"] = { r = 0.80, g = 0.00, b = 0.00 }, ["Magic"] = { r = 0.20, g = 0.60, b = 1.00 }, ["Curse"] = { r = 0.60, g = 0.00, b = 1.00 }, ["Disease"] = { r = 0.60, g = 0.40, b = 0.00 }, ["Poison"] = { r = 0.00, g = 0.60, b = 0.00 }, }
-- SecondsToTimeAbbrev + its GlobalStrings (UIParent.lua l.1034 / GlobalStrings.lua). We load -- no UIParent/GlobalStrings, so define them here (guarded, in case a later file ships them). DAY_ONELETTER_ABBR = DAY_ONELETTER_ABBR or "%d d" HOUR_ONELETTER_ABBR = HOUR_ONELETTER_ABBR or "%d h" MINUTE_ONELETTER_ABBR = MINUTE_ONELETTER_ABBR or "%d m" SECOND_ONELETTER_ABBR = SECOND_ONELETTER_ABBR or "%d s"
if not SecondsToTimeAbbrev then function SecondsToTimeAbbrev(seconds) if seconds > 86400 then return format(DAY_ONELETTER_ABBR, ceil(seconds / 86400)) elseif seconds > 3600 then return format(HOUR_ONELETTER_ABBR, ceil(seconds / 3600)) elseif seconds > 60 then return format(MINUTE_ONELETTER_ABBR, ceil(seconds / 60)) end return format(SECOND_ONELETTER_ABBR, seconds) end end
-- The frame-wide flash pulse (BuffFrame_OnLoad / _OnUpdate, BuffFrame.lua l.17-56). One -- BUFF_ALPHA_VALUE is computed per frame and every low-on-time button reads it, so they blink -- in unison. The bar also seats each duration string under its button here. function BuffFrame_OnLoad() BuffFrameUpdateTime = 0 BuffFrameFlashTime = 0 BuffFrameFlashState = 1 BUFF_ALPHA_VALUE = 1 for i = 0, 23 do getglobal("BuffButton" .. i .. "Duration"):SetPoint("TOP", "BuffButton" .. i, "BOTTOM", 0, 0) end end
-- Half of the square wave, run down by one frame. BuffFrameFlashTime is the time LEFT in -- the current half; when it goes under, the state flips and the counter reloads with the -- new half's length. The overshoot is carried into that half — unless it is longer than -- the half itself, in which case the whole period is kept rather than skipped, so a -- stalled frame costs at most one beat of drift instead of racing the pulse forward. local function buffFlashAdvance(elapsed) BuffFrameFlashTime = BuffFrameFlashTime - elapsed if BuffFrameFlashTime >= 0 then return end local overtime = -BuffFrameFlashTime if BuffFrameFlashState == 0 then BuffFrameFlashState = 1 BuffFrameFlashTime = BUFF_FLASH_TIME_ON else BuffFrameFlashState = 0 BuffFrameFlashTime = BUFF_FLASH_TIME_OFF end if overtime < BuffFrameFlashTime then BuffFrameFlashTime = BuffFrameFlashTime - overtime end end
function BuffFrame_OnUpdate(elapsed) -- The tooltip re-poll's throttle (ref l.29-33): oscillates around zero with a -- TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME period, and BuffButton_OnUpdate refreshes a hovered plate only on -- the frames it is non-positive. ActionBar.xml declares TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME and loads -- first (benilla.toc), so it is always a number by the time this runs. if BuffFrameUpdateTime > 0 then BuffFrameUpdateTime = BuffFrameUpdateTime - elapsed else BuffFrameUpdateTime = BuffFrameUpdateTime + TOOLTIP_UPDATE_TIME end
-- The pulse's level for this frame: a 0..1 ramp up across the ON half and back down -- across the OFF half (both scaled by BUFF_FLASH_TIME_ON — the reference's own choice, -- and invisible while the two halves are the same length), squashed into -- [BUFF_MIN_ALPHA, 1] so a warning icon dims rather than disappears. -- -- Computed into a LOCAL and published once. BUFF_ALPHA_VALUE is read by every visible -- button, so it is not scratch space: the reference assigns the raw ramp to it and then -- squashes it in a second statement, which leaves the global holding an un-squashed -- value for the length of one statement. buffFlashAdvance(elapsed) local level if BuffFrameFlashState == 1 then level = (BUFF_FLASH_TIME_ON - BuffFrameFlashTime) / BUFF_FLASH_TIME_ON else level = BuffFrameFlashTime / BUFF_FLASH_TIME_ON end BUFF_ALPHA_VALUE = (level * (1 - BUFF_MIN_ALPHA)) + BUFF_MIN_ALPHA end
-- BuffButtons_UpdatePositions (BuffFrame.lua l.152-160): the ROW PITCH depends on whether a -- timer sits under each icon. Shown, the three rows land at y = 0/−45/−90 (a 30px icon + a -- 15px gutter); hidden, at 0/−35/−70 — the icons close up to the same 5px the columns use. -- The anchors are the reference's own, through the TempEnchant chain: row 2 hangs off -- TempEnchant1 and row 3 off TemporaryEnchantFrame, which is what keeps them still while the -- top row slides left to clear an equipped enchant. SetPoint on a point already held -- overwrites it (layout.rs — the client's own SetPoint law). -- -- This is the Buff Durations row's `applyFunc`, and the ONLY thing the setting needs applied: -- the timer text itself is re-decided every frame by the poll below, so a click changes what -- the next frame draws without anyone telling it. Geometry is the part that is stated once. function BuffButtons_UpdatePositions() if SHOW_BUFF_DURATIONS == "1" then BuffButton8:SetPoint("TOP", "TempEnchant1", "BOTTOM", 0, -15) BuffButton16:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "TemporaryEnchantFrame", "TOPRIGHT", 0, -90) else BuffButton8:SetPoint("TOP", "TempEnchant1", "BOTTOM", 0, -5) BuffButton16:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "TemporaryEnchantFrame", "TOPRIGHT", 0, -70) end end
-- Void a button's memory of what its duration region last had WRITTEN to it (the -- benillaDur* fields BuffFrame_UpdateDuration gates on). Called by everything ELSE that -- touches the region — the aura event's repaint here, the enchant row's clear — so the -- per-frame gate can never skip a write against a region somebody moved under it; a -- forgotten state just means the next poll writes once. local function buffDurationForget(button) button.benillaDurShown = nil button.benillaDurText = nil button.benillaDurWarn = nil button.benillaDurSetting = nil end
-- The button's aura, resolved on the discrete-change edge and CACHED AS A POSITION -- (ref BuffButton_Update, l.58-107). `this:GetID()` is the 0-based ordinal within -- this.buffFilter; buffIndex is the cache position every read below uses. function BuffButton_Update() local buffIndex, untilCancelled = GetPlayerBuff(this:GetID(), this.buffFilter) this.buffIndex = buffIndex this.untilCancelled = untilCancelled local buffDuration = this.durationFS or getglobal(this:GetName() .. "Duration") this.durationFS = buffDuration
-- -1, not nil: the miss sentinel the whole family agrees on. if buffIndex < 0 then this:Hide() buffDuration:Hide() buffDurationForget(this) return end this:SetAlpha(1.0) this.benillaLastAlpha = 1.0 this:Show() if SHOW_BUFF_DURATIONS == "1" then buffDuration:Show() else buffDuration:Hide() end buffDurationForget(this)
getglobal(this:GetName() .. "Icon"):SetTexture(GetPlayerBuffTexture(buffIndex) or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON)
-- Debuff border, tinted by dispel class (harmful buttons only — helpful ones have no -- $parentBorder, so getglobal is nil and the whole lookup is skipped; see the header). local debuffSlot = getglobal(this:GetName() .. "Border") if debuffSlot then local debuffType = GetPlayerBuffDispelType(GetPlayerBuff(this:GetID(), "HARMFUL")) local color = DebuffTypeColor[debuffType] or DebuffTypeColor["none"] debuffSlot:SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) end
-- Stack count, shown only above 1 (ref l.94-102). GetPlayerBuffApplications is a NUMBER -- on every path — 1 for an absent position — so `> 1` needs no nil guard. local buffCount = getglobal(this:GetName() .. "Count") local count = GetPlayerBuffApplications(buffIndex) if count > 1 then buffCount:SetText(count) else buffCount:SetText("") end
if GameTooltip and GameTooltip:IsOwned(this) then GameTooltip:SetPlayerBuff(buffIndex) end end
-- A button takes right-clicks and listens for the aura rebuild. The first paint hides it -- until the feed reports an aura. PLAYER_AURAS_CHANGED is the reference's event and the app -- fires it beside the Era-shaped UNIT_AURA on the same rebuild (`ui_aura`). function BuffButton_OnLoad() -- Valid tokens for "buffFilter": HELPFUL, HARMFUL, CANCELABLE, NOT_CANCELABLE. Note the -- mask starts at ZERO once a filter string is given, so a bare "CANCELABLE" would match -- nothing — the sign must always be named. BuffButton_Update() this:RegisterForClicks("RightButtonUp") this:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_AURAS_CHANGED") end
function BuffButton_OnEvent(event) if event == "PLAYER_AURAS_CHANGED" then BuffButton_Update() end end
-- Per-frame: RE-READ the remaining time from the cached POSITION (never a cached duration), -- flash in the last 31s, write the abbreviated timer, and tick a hovered tooltip. -- -- The re-read every frame is the reference's own shape, and it is load-bearing: a duration -- that changes without any discrete change — a recast, a DoT reapplied, cast pushback, the -- server's replay of every duration at world entry — fires no aura event, so a button that -- cached its expiry on the event would keep counting the OLD one down, sit at "0 s" while -- the buff is still live, and never show a timer for an aura whose duration landed after -- its icon did. Both were live defects; the poll is what makes them unrepresentable -- (decision 0846). -- -- The untilCancelled early-out (ref l.124-127) is what keeps a permanent aura from flashing -- a "0 s" countdown while waiting for a duration packet that is never coming: it is answered -- from the SPELL, so it is right before any packet arrives. This frame runs only on visible -- frames (`UiScript::tick`), exactly as the client's does, so a hidden button's stale -- buffIndex is never read. function BuffButton_OnUpdate() local button = this -- A permanent aura has nothing to count down and nothing to flash toward, so it is -- done in one line: UpdateDuration with no time left is exactly "hide the timer", -- which is the whole of the reference's early-out here. (The reference reaches for the -- $parentDuration region itself to do it, on every frame of every visible button, and -- then throws that region away and lets UpdateDuration look it up again.) if button.untilCancelled == 1 then BuffFrame_UpdateDuration(button, nil) return end
local buffIndex = button.buffIndex local timeLeft = GetPlayerBuffTimeLeft(buffIndex) -- The flash is NOT gated on the timer setting: the reference pulses a button in its last -- 31s whether or not a number is drawn under it, and with the timers off it is the only -- thing left saying "about to drop". -- -- Written only when it moves (decision 1396's class — a settled bar must not rewrite -- per frame what changes only on an edge). Inside the warning window BUFF_ALPHA_VALUE -- is a fresh ramp value every frame, so the pulse flows through the compare untouched; -- outside it the value is the 1.0 that is already there, forever. local alpha if timeLeft < BUFF_WARNING_TIME then alpha = BUFF_ALPHA_VALUE else alpha = 1.0 end if alpha ~= button.benillaLastAlpha then button.benillaLastAlpha = alpha button:SetAlpha(alpha) end
BuffFrame_UpdateDuration(button, timeLeft)
-- A tooltip we own is re-read on the throttle's beat, not every frame. if BuffFrameUpdateTime <= 0 and GameTooltip and GameTooltip:IsOwned(button) then GameTooltip:SetPlayerBuff(buffIndex) end end
-- Right-click cancels by CACHE POSITION (ref l.148-150). The app sends CMSG_CANCEL_AURA for -- a cancelable aura and drops the rest, so a debuff right-click is a silent no-op. function BuffButton_OnClick() CancelPlayerBuff(this.buffIndex) end
-- Clear enchant slots `first`..2 — the tail of the row nothing is using this frame. The -- Hide moves the Duration region under the poll's write gate, so the gate's memory is -- voided with it. local function buffEnchantClear(first) for slot = first, 2 do local button = getglobal("TempEnchant" .. slot) button:Hide() getglobal("TempEnchant" .. slot .. "Duration"):Hide() buffDurationForget(button) end end
-- One hand's six steps (the same block the reference spells out twice, ref l.180-207): -- an enchanted hand packs into the next slot rightwards and keeps its countdown and -- warning pulse live; a bare hand packs nothing. Returns the new fill count. A plain -- function of its arguments so the per-frame path allocates nothing — this used to be a -- two-row table built fresh every frame. -- -- `slot` is the live API's inventory id, which is also what the button's hover reads -- back off itself to ask for the ITEM's tooltip. local function buffEnchantHand(filled, enchanted, expiration, slot) if not enchanted then return filled end filled = filled + 1 local button = getglobal("TempEnchant" .. filled) button:SetID(slot) getglobal(button:GetName() .. "Icon"):SetTexture( GetInventoryItemTexture("player", slot) or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) button:Show()
-- The wire counts an enchant down in MILLISECONDS; everything the row draws is -- in seconds. A nil expiration is "no countdown known", which the timer and the -- warning flash both read as "nothing to warn about". local timeLeft = expiration and (expiration / 1000) BuffFrame_UpdateDuration(button, timeLeft) if timeLeft and timeLeft < BUFF_WARNING_TIME then button:SetAlpha(BUFF_ALPHA_VALUE) else button:SetAlpha(1.0) end return filled end
-- The temporary-weapon-enchant row (ref l.162-233). GetWeaponEnchantInfo is the whole data -- path: two flags, two remaining-MILLISECOND counts, two charge counts (the charges are -- read by nobody here, and are named only to spell the API's shape out). -- -- OFF HAND FIRST is the part that matters: the row packs from slot 1 rightwards, so with -- both weapons enchanted the main hand lands in slot 2 and therefore sits to the LEFT of -- the off hand. function BuffFrame_Enchant_OnUpdate(elapsed) local hasMainHandEnchant, mainHandExpiration, mainHandCharges, hasOffHandEnchant, offHandExpiration, offHandCharges = GetWeaponEnchantInfo()
-- Nothing enchanted: clear the whole row and park BuffFrame back on its resting -- point — ONCE per transition, latched on benillaCleared (decision 1396's class: -- re-deriving per frame what changes only on an edge). The latch starts unset, so -- the FIRST pass still writes — the load-time hide the header's TempEnchant note -- leans on — and any enchant appearing clears it below. if not hasMainHandEnchant and not hasOffHandEnchant then if not TemporaryEnchantFrame.benillaCleared then TemporaryEnchantFrame.benillaCleared = true -- Forget the last row width too: after a park, the next enchanted pass must -- re-write the width AND the bar's TOPLEFT anchor whatever its fill count is. TemporaryEnchantFrame.benillaFilled = nil buffEnchantClear(1) BuffFrame:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "TemporaryEnchantFrame", "TOPRIGHT", 0, 0) end return end TemporaryEnchantFrame.benillaCleared = nil
local filled = buffEnchantHand(0, hasOffHandEnchant, offHandExpiration, 17) filled = buffEnchantHand(filled, hasMainHandEnchant, mainHandExpiration, 16) buffEnchantClear(filled + 1)
-- Position buff frame: the row is `filled` icons wide, and the bar starts one 5px -- gutter to its left. The geometry depends on nothing but `filled`, so it is written -- only when that changes. if TemporaryEnchantFrame.benillaFilled ~= filled then TemporaryEnchantFrame.benillaFilled = filled TemporaryEnchantFrame:SetWidth(filled * 32) BuffFrame:SetPoint("TOPRIGHT", "TemporaryEnchantFrame", "TOPLEFT", -5, 0) end end
function BuffFrame_EnchantButton_OnUpdate() if GameTooltip and GameTooltip:IsOwned(this) then BuffFrame_EnchantButton_OnEnter() end end
-- The enchant hover is the ITEM's tooltip, not an aura's — the plate hangs below-left like -- the buff buttons' (ref l.242-245). function BuffFrame_EnchantButton_OnEnter() if not GameTooltip then return end GameTooltip:SetOwner(this, "ANCHOR_BOTTOMLEFT") GameTooltip:SetInventoryItem("player", this:GetID()) end
-- BuffFrame_UpdateDuration (ref l.247-260), gate and all: the timer draws only when the -- setting is on AND there is a live one. `timeLeft` nil is the enchant row's "no countdown -- known" case. Hidden, not blanked — see the header's deviation note. -- -- The POLL stays per-frame (the re-read is load-bearing — decision 0846); only the WRITES -- are gated, on what was last written: shown, the abbreviated text, the warning band, and -- the SHOW_BUFF_DURATIONS value itself (so the settings toggle stays live). Deliberately -- never on a measured extent (1396's trap: a fixture with no font engine measures 0 -- forever); the compare is against the STRING this function computed, nothing the host -- had to shape. The benillaDur* memory is voided by whoever else touches the region -- (buffDurationForget), so a stale skip is unrepresentable. function BuffFrame_UpdateDuration(buffButton, timeLeft) local duration = buffButton.durationFS or getglobal(buffButton:GetName() .. "Duration") buffButton.durationFS = duration local setting = SHOW_BUFF_DURATIONS -- Two ways to have no number to draw: the setting is off, or nothing has told us how -- long is left (the enchant row's "no countdown known"). if setting ~= "1" or not timeLeft then -- == false, not falsey: nil is "no memory", and the first pass must write. if buffButton.benillaDurShown == false and buffButton.benillaDurSetting == setting then return end buffButton.benillaDurShown = false buffButton.benillaDurText = nil buffButton.benillaDurWarn = nil buffButton.benillaDurSetting = setting duration:Hide() return end local text = SecondsToTimeAbbrev(timeLeft) -- Gold most of the way, white inside the last minute — the number's own warning, a -- half-minute ahead of the icon starting to pulse. local warning = timeLeft < BUFF_DURATION_WARNING_TIME if buffButton.benillaDurShown == true and buffButton.benillaDurText == text and buffButton.benillaDurWarn == warning and buffButton.benillaDurSetting == setting then return end buffButton.benillaDurShown = true buffButton.benillaDurText = text buffButton.benillaDurWarn = warning buffButton.benillaDurSetting = setting duration:SetText(text) local color = NORMAL_FONT_COLOR if warning then color = HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR end duration:SetVertexColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) duration:Show() end

Scripts.OnEnter: if GameTooltip then GameTooltip:SetOwner(this, "ANCHOR_BOTTOMLEFT") GameTooltip:SetPlayerBuff(this.buffIndex) end
